text:
Priya (Finance): Quick note: launching a 'buffered quota' behavior next week that lets short spikes avoid immediate hard throttles and adds a line-item on invoices so customers can see any buffered consumption. Pilot starts Tue.

Owen (Product): Does this change SDK behavior or is it server-only?

Priya (Finance): Server-only. SDKs will still surface 429s when hard throttles happen; during a short buffered window clients may not receive a 429 for bursts under 20-30s. We'll document expected behaviors.

Zara (Support): Need canned responses for customers asking why their token usage looked higher than expected.

Priya (Finance): Draft blurb: "Short bursts may be temporarily absorbed by a buffer; you'll see 'buffered_tokens' under Usage adjustments. Only persistent overage is billed as usual."

Ravi (Eng): Runtime note: per-key sliding window + per-route opt-outs. Metrics: `buffered_tokens_total` and `buffer_suppressed_count`. Expose in Console and metrics API. Canary to 8% traffic Wed 02:00 UTC; rollback if error-rate +0.75% or tail-latency +30ms.

billing-bot: Invoice example under Usage adjustments:

```
Usage adjustments:
  base_tokens: 5,120,900
  overage_tokens: 4,200
  buffered_tokens: 600
  billed_overage_tokens: 3,600
```

Zara (Support): I'll prep KB + dispute flow; request final FAQ by Monday 9am PT.

Owen (Product): We'll include an opt-in checkbox for startup pilot accounts and a per-route toggle in Console.

Priya (Finance): Action items: Owen 1 provide customer copy by Mon 9am PT; Ravi 1 dashboards and metrics by canary; Zara 1 KB & dispute flow. Leaving thread open for updates.
